item.title: A Little-Known Election Is Coming That Will Affect How the UN Spends Its Money, So Pay Attention
item.description: United Nations member states are scheduled to elect 10 new countries on Nov. 6 to the advisory committee on budgets, a 21-member body that holds immense influence over the organization’s finances but operates under the radar. Everyone needs to pay attention to the vote. The ACABQ, or Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, provides ... Read more

item.title: Ethiopia: Violence in the north is pushing health system to the brink, WHO chief warns
item.description: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

item.title: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
item.description: Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.

item.title: World News in Brief: healthcare crisis in Yemen’s Taiz and Afghanistan, Western Sahara mission's phased closure
item.description: The humanitarian crisis in Yemen is worsening, particularly in the southwestern city of Taiz, which is being encircled by paramilitary Iran-backed Houthi forces.

item.title: Ukraine: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
item.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.

item.title: New Biodiversity Funding Brings Hope for Armenia’s Lake Sevan
item.description: In the second article on finance mobilisation and new funding commitments, IPS looks at how funding moves from the GEF to local communities and supports biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration on the ground.

item.title: The Commonwealth Has 2.7 Billion Reasons to Act
item.description: Commonwealth countries are facing many challenges at their biennial meeting in Antigua this week. We are determined to change course.

item.title: WFP Warnings Become a Reality as Food Insecurity in Haiti on Track to Reach Record Highs
item.description: Warnings by the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) that Haiti’s fragile food security gains could quickly unravel are becoming a reality. item.title: The UN Human Rights Council at 20: Credibility in Question
item.description: On 13 October, Burundi won a second consecutive term on the UN Human Rights Council, the UN’s main human rights body. The CIVICUS Monitor rates civic space in Burundi as closed, the worst category.
